phoenix_code_evaluator_context.description: This guidance applies when the user is creating or editing a code evaluator in the UI, i.e., when `ui_contexts` has a `codeEvaluator` entry. A code evaluator is a Python or TypeScript function named `evaluate` that receives some subset of `input`, `output`, `reference`, and `metadata` and returns a score or label. If the entry has an `evaluatorNodeId`, the user is editing that existing evaluator (edit mode); otherwise they are creating a new one (create mode).
phoenix_code_evaluator_context.draft_contract: - The evaluator function in `sourceCode` must be named exactly `evaluate`. Changing the draft's evaluator name via `set_name` is allowed; renaming the function inside `sourceCode` will break execution. - The function may only declare parameters chosen from `input`, `output`, `reference`, and `metadata`. - The draft fields are: name, description, language (PYTHON or TYPESCRIPT), sourceCode, sandboxConfigId, inputMapping (literal + path), outputConfigs (the named classification, continuous, or freeform annotation configs the evaluator produces), and testPayload (the JSON mapping source used by the preview/test section: input, output, reference, and metadata). - In edit mode, language is immutable — it was fixed when the evaluator was created and is tied to the sandbox configuration. Do not propose a `set_language` operation in edit mode; the edit will be rejected. - The selected sandboxConfigId must match the draft language. In create mode, the draft must keep a non-null sandboxConfigId. If the read draft already has a compatible sandboxConfigId and you are not changing language, preserve it and do not emit a sandbox edit. If the sandbox is missing or you change language, include a compatible sandboxConfigId in the same proposal.
phoenix_code_evaluator_context.available_sandbox_configs: The selectable sandbox inventory is not inlined here. To pick a `sandboxConfigId`, call `ui.evaluators.code.read({})` — its output's `availableSandboxConfigs` (id, name, language, backendType) is already filtered to the selectable set; choose the entry whose `language` matches the draft language. Do not query the API for this list. Fall back to the `bash` tool's `phoenix-gql` command only when you need authoring constraints the read does not carry (runtime dialect notes, env vars, internet access, dependencies): query `sandboxBackends { backendType status languageDialect runtimeNotes }` and `sandboxProviders { backendType enabled configs { id name language enabled config { envVars { name } internetAccess { mode } dependencies { packages } } } }`, keeping only configs whose provider `enabled` is true, config `enabled` is true, and backend `status` is `AVAILABLE`. Treat `languageDialect` and `runtimeNotes` as the runtime's authoring constraints, and the config's environment variables, internet access, and packages as what the evaluator can do: a sandbox with model credentials and internet access can call a model from code, so a composite, jury, or pairwise judgment can be a code evaluator there. Request only `envVars { name }` — never `secretKey`.
phoenix_code_evaluator_context.guidance: Before authoring or revising this evaluator, `load_skill` the `phoenix-evaluator-design` skill, then call `ui.evaluators.code.read({})` in an `execute_browser_action` script — e.g. `const draft = await ui.evaluators.code.read({}); return draft;` — and read its `testPayload`: it is a real example from the dataset, and its `input`, `output`, and `metadata` are the record shape the plan must name. Only then write (or, when resuming, `cat`) the plan file as `evaluator_authoring` describes; under `manual` edit permission, wait for the user to approve the plan before the first `ui.evaluators.code.edit`. This form builds code evaluators only. When the plan's `Type` comes out as an LLM judge (the judgment needs reading comprehension, not a computation), do not force it into code here: say so, and hand off to the LLM evaluator form (`[Create LLM evaluator](/datasets/<datasetNodeId>/evaluators?createLlmEvaluator=true)`, or `ui.evaluators.llm.openForm({})` from a dataset-backed playground) as `phoenix_dataset_context` describes, carrying the plan file over. Seed the preview from the plan's calibration cases with `set_test_payload`, one case per `ui.evaluators.code.test`, keeping the form's own `testPayload` as the first (real) case and shaping invented cases exactly like it. Each test's result arrives as `results[].annotation` (`label`, `score`, `explanation`); record it in the plan.
phoenix_code_evaluator_context.editing_the_draft:
Whether you may propose form edits depends on whether a `viewer_access` block is present in your instructions and, in create mode, on the sandbox inventory:
Do not propose form edits; answer from the readable draft and explain that persistence requires edit access.
Read the draft first and check its `availableSandboxConfigs` (see `available_sandbox_configs`). If it is empty, do not propose form edits; direct the user to `/settings/sandboxes` to enable a sandbox provider first. Otherwise call `ui.evaluators.code.edit` to show the user an accept/reject diff before changing the form, including `set_test_payload` when the preview payload should change.
Call `ui.evaluators.code.edit` to show the user an accept/reject diff before changing the form, including `set_test_payload` when the preview payload should change.

case.condition: edit access and edit_permission is bypass

testing_the_draft.case: Auto-accept is on: once the draft is populated and valid, call `ui.evaluators.code.test({})` to preview it (revise the source or `testPayload` and re-test if the preview surfaces a problem) — do this without pausing to ask the user for confirmation.

case.condition: edit access and edit_permission is manual

testing_the_draft.case: After the user accepts a populated draft, offer to run `ui.evaluators.code.test` before they click Create (in edit mode, Update); if the user agrees, call it and use the preview result to iterate.

case.condition: view-only access or the sandbox inventory is empty

testing_the_draft.case: Do not offer a draft test; the `ui.evaluators.code.test` operation cannot run without a usable sandbox.

case.condition: edit_permission is bypass and draft edits are allowed

persisting_the_draft.case: Once the plan's results show every calibration case matching, persist by calling `ui.evaluators.code.submit({})` in its own `execute_browser_action` script, after the plan file has been rewritten with the observed results — never in the script that ran the tests. It runs the same validated save the Create button does (in edit mode, Update) and returns the committed evaluator. Drive the flow through to this save without stopping to ask; report the evaluator as saved only from that operation's success result, and do not tell the user to click Create or Update themselves.

case.condition: edit_permission is manual or draft edits are not allowed

persisting_the_draft.case: Do not claim the evaluator is persisted; persistence remains the user's Create action (in edit mode, Update) in the form.
